sentences.en: As wildfire seasons grow longer and deadlier, states are increasingly relying on private companies to provide thousands of firefighters to the front lines.
sentences.zh: 随着野火季越来越长、越来越致命，各州越来越依赖私营公司来提供数千名前线消防员。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Hannah Dreyer explains how lax rules and regulatory loopholes have left many of these firefighters sick, in debt, and on their own.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事汉娜·德赖厄将为我们解释，宽松的规则和监管漏洞如何让许多消防员身患重病、负债累累且孤立无援。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, October 28th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月28日，星期二。

sentences.en: Hannah, it feels like every year there are more and more wildfires and you have spent months investigating one specific aspect of wildfires,
sentences.zh: 汉娜，感觉每年野火都越来越多，你花了几个月时间调查野火的一个特定方面，

sentences.en: which is the wildfire fighting industry.
sentences.zh: 也就是野火扑救行业。

sentences.en: So I'd love to start off with you telling us what got you interested in that particular angle.
sentences.zh: 所以我很想从你开始，跟我们讲讲是什么让你对这个特定角度产生兴趣的。

sentences.en: I first started thinking about this after the fires that tore through Los Angeles in January.
sentences.zh: 我是从一月份席卷洛杉矶的大火之后开始思考这个问题的。

sentences.en: I saw that there was all this footage, all these pictures coming in of the people who were fighting those fires.
sentences.zh: 我看到有各种各样的现场视频和照片传出来，拍的都是那些正在扑灭大火的人。

sentences.en: And I couldn't help but notice that there were all of these firefighters out there standing in what looked like the most toxic black smoke and none of them were wearing masks.
sentences.zh: 我不禁注意到，有那么多消防员站在看起来毒性极强的黑烟里，而且他们都没有戴口罩。

sentences.en: And it got me wondering why is that and what might be the consequences of working in that kind of environment with no protection.
sentences.zh: 这让我开始纳闷，为什么会这样，在那种没有任何防护的环境下工作会有什么后果。

sentences.en: And so I started digging into the industry of people who fight wildfires.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始深入挖掘扑灭野火的人员所在的这个行业。

sentences.en: And what I discovered is that it's completely unlike any industry.
sentences.zh: 而我发现的是，它完全不像任何其他行业。

sentences.en: They are out there in these really hazardous conditions and they work without protection.
sentences.zh: 他们在那些极其危险的条件下工作，却没有任何防护。

sentences.en: And a lot of them are getting very sick at young ages.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有很多人在很年轻的时候就病得很重。

sentences.en: And when they develop things like severe lung damage or cancer, things that are linked to this smoke exposure, they're often on their own.
sentences.zh: 当他们出现严重肺损伤或癌症等与接触烟雾相关的病症时，他们往往只能自生自灭。

sentences.en: Often they don't even have basic health insurance.
sentences.zh: 通常他们甚至连基本的健康保险都没有。

sentences.en: So basically they're vulnerable at several different stages of this process, from starting work to actually getting sick.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上他们在整个过程的几个不同阶段都是脆弱的，从开始工作到真正生病。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, what a lot of people have told me is they feel like they put their health on the line to protect people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很多人对我说过，他们觉得自己是为了保护人们而将健康置于危险之中。

sentences.en: And then when they get sick themselves, there's sort of no one there protecting them.
sentences.zh: 然后当他们自己生病时，却基本上没有人去保护他们。

sentences.en: And this is not a small issue.
sentences.zh: 而且这不是一个小问题。

sentences.en: There are tens of thousands of people who do this work almost year round now.
sentences.zh: 现在有成千上万的人几乎全年都在做这项工作。

sentences.en: And as wildfire season grows longer and gets more intense, this is something that is just going to become more and more urgent.
sentences.zh: 随着野火季越来越长、强度越来越大，这只会变得越来越紧迫。

sentences.en: So to get my arms around this, I talked to hundreds of firefighters.
sentences.zh: 为了弄清这全貌，我采访了数百名消防员。

sentences.en: Many of them were very sick.
sentences.zh: 他们当中有许多人病得很重。

sentences.en: But there was one story that really stood out to me.
sentences.zh: 但有一个故事真正触动了我。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 嗨。

sentences.en: Come on in.
sentences.zh: 请进。

sentences.en: I'm Matt.
sentences.zh: 我是马特。

sentences.en: I'm Joel's dad.
sentences.zh: 我是乔尔的爸爸。

sentences.en: This is a young man named Joel Eisminger.
sentences.zh: 这是一个名叫乔尔·艾斯明格的年轻小伙子。

sentences.en: So can we go all the way back to your childhood and start there?
sentences.zh: 那我们能一直追溯到你的童年，从那里开始吗？

sentences.en: Just a lot of riding bicycles and a lot of races.
sentences.zh: 就是骑了很多自行车，参加了很多比赛。

sentences.en: Joel was a shy kid who moved around a lot.
sentences.zh: 乔尔是个害羞的孩子，搬过很多次家。

sentences.en: He didn't always have an easy time making friends.
sentences.zh: 他交朋友并不总是一帆风顺。

sentences.en: He was really physical.
sentences.zh: 他非常好动。

sentences.en: He went on long hikes, long bike rides.
sentences.zh: 他去进行长途徒步、长途骑行。

sentences.en: He played lacrosse in high school, and his nickname was Battering Ram.
sentences.zh: 他在高中打长曲棍球，他的外号叫“撞城槌”。

sentences.en: But he had a hard time focusing in school.
sentences.zh: 但他在学校很难集中注意力。

sentences.en: Sometimes he didn't go to class.
sentences.zh: 有时候他不去上课。

sentences.en: He sort of barely managed to graduate.
sentences.zh: 他可以说是勉强才毕了业。

sentences.en: And once he graduated, he wasn't sure what he was going to do.
sentences.zh: 一旦毕业了，他就不确定自己要做什么。

sentences.en: Uh, got a job at Taco Bell.
sentences.zh: 呃，在塔可钟找了份工作。

sentences.en: He was living in Oregon.
sentences.zh: 他当时住在俄勒冈州。

sentences.en: He got a job at Taco Bell.
sentences.zh: 他在塔可钟找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: And one night...
sentences.zh: 有一天晚上……

sentences.en: I watched a movie called Only the Brave.
sentences.zh: 我看了一部名为《勇往直前》的电影。

sentences.en: I work this blaze near Big Timber, Montana.
sentences.zh: 我在蒙大拿州大蒂伯附近的那场大火中工作。

sentences.en: He started watching this movie on TV called Only the Brave.
sentences.zh: 他开始在电视上看这部名叫《勇往直前》的电影。

sentences.en: No matter what's going on, we can't go back up there.
sentences.zh: 不管发生什么，我们都不能再回上面去了。

sentences.en: Stay together.
sentences.zh: 待在一起。

sentences.en: It's a movie that's about this tragedy that happened a few years ago, where basically an entire crew of wildland firefighters died burned by a fire.
sentences.zh: 这是一部关于几年前发生的悲剧的电影，基本上是一整支森林消防队员队伍在一场大火中殉职。

sentences.en: Hey, Soup, I just wanted to thank you for pulling me out earlier.
sentences.zh: 嘿，苏普，我只是想谢谢你刚才把我拉出来。

sentences.en: It was definitely an ass pucker, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 那绝对让人吓得屁滚尿流，对吧？

sentences.en: No doubt, man.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，老兄。

sentences.en: I thought I was dying.
sentences.zh: 我以为我要死了。

sentences.en: And it's this tragic movie.
sentences.zh: 这是一部悲剧电影。

sentences.en: But his reaction to it was to focus on the bond between these crew members.
sentences.zh: 但他的反应却是关注这些队员之间的羁绊。

sentences.en: This ain't the greatest job in the world.
sentences.zh: 这不是世界上最棒的工作。

sentences.en: I don't know what is.
sentences.zh: 我不知道什么才是。

sentences.en: So in the movie, these guys are always joking.
sentences.zh: 所以在电影里，这些家伙总是在开玩笑。

sentences.en: They're really close.
sentences.zh: 他们的关系非常亲密。

sentences.en: And that really appealed to Joel.
sentences.zh: 这深深地吸引了乔尔。

sentences.en: I mean, he's working at, like, a fast food restaurant during the day.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他白天在一家快餐店之类的地方工作。

sentences.en: And to him, this is like, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这就像是，哦，天哪。

sentences.en: It's a way to be outside, have friends, and be doing what he's best at, which is this sort of, like, physical work.
sentences.zh: 这是一种可以去户外、拥有朋友并做他最擅长的事情的方式，也就是这种体力活。

sentences.en: So the very next day, he goes and applies to work for a company called Pacific Oasis.
sentences.zh: 所以就在第二天，他去申请了一家名为“太平洋绿洲”的公司的职位。

sentences.en: And what's Pacific Oasis?
sentences.zh: 什么是“太平洋绿洲”？

sentences.en: Pacific Oasis is one of hundreds of companies that now offer private firefighting services to the federal government.
sentences.zh: “太平洋绿洲”是为联邦政府提供私人消防服务的数百家公司之一。

sentences.en: And these are easier jobs to get than working directly for the federal government doing firefighting.
sentences.zh: 比起直接为联邦政府做消防工作，这些工作更容易得到。

sentences.en: Like less red tape?
sentences.zh: 比如繁文缛节更少？

sentences.en: Yeah, less paperwork to fill out, fewer hoops to jump through.
sentences.zh: 对，需要填写的表格更少，需要跨过的门槛更少。

sentences.en: You can get hired on the spot.
sentences.zh: 你可以当场被录用。

sentences.en: And so they attract a lot of people like Joel, who maybe were a little adrift in life.
sentences.zh: 所以它们吸引了许多像乔尔这样的人，他们可能在生活中有点随波逐流。

sentences.en: So it's an easier job to get than working for the federal government.
sentences.zh: 所以这比为联邦政府工作更容易得到这份工作。

sentences.en: But there's a tradeoff, which is that there are a lot fewer protections and fewer benefits.
sentences.zh: 但天下没有免费的午餐，那就是保障和福利要少得多。

sentences.en: So most people working for these companies don't have health insurance, for example.
sentences.zh: 因此，为这些公司工作的绝大多数人都没有健康保险，比如说。

sentences.en: They have less training.
sentences.zh: 他们的培训较少。

sentences.en: And overall, they're just sort of less protected.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，他们受到的保护就是比较少。

sentences.en: So at Taco Bell, I had a manager.
sentences.zh: 所以在塔可钟的时候，我有一个经理。

sentences.en: He brought up Pacific Oasis, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他提到了“太平洋绿洲”。

sentences.en: So, like, I had that in my head already.
sentences.zh: 所以，我脑子里已经有这个概念了。

sentences.en: And he just told me all the cool stories.
sentences.zh: 他只是跟我讲了所有那些酷炫的故事。

sentences.en: And I was like, oh, this is sweet, man.
sentences.zh: 我就想，哦，这太棒了，老兄。

sentences.en: You know?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: He's like, oh, I'll hire anybody.
sentences.zh: 他就像是，哦，谁我都雇。

sentences.en: So Joel walks in the door.
sentences.zh: 于是乔尔走进了大门。

sentences.en: He meets with the president of the company.
sentences.zh: 他见到了公司的总裁。

sentences.en: He's like, this is exactly what we're looking for.
sentences.zh: 他就像是，这正是我们在找的人。

sentences.en: And signs him up for training.
sentences.zh: 并让他报名参加培训。

sentences.en: Straight away.
sentences.zh: 马上。

sentences.en: On the spot.
sentences.zh: 当场。

sentences.en: And he's almost immediately sent out to a major fire.
sentences.zh: 他几乎立刻就被派去扑救一场大火。

sentences.en: And he's still 18 at this point.
sentences.zh: 而他此时年仅18岁。

sentences.en: His father, Matt, remembers driving him down to the Pacific Oasis headquarters.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲马特还记得开车送他去“太平洋绿洲”总部的情景。

sentences.en: So I went down there with him and dropped him off at the fire like it was a sporting event.
sentences.zh: 所以我跟他一起去了，把他送到火场，就像送去参加体育赛事一样。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: And I was incredibly worried about him, of course, as I think most parents would be.
sentences.zh: 当然，我极其担心他，我想大多数父母都会这样。

sentences.en: Matt was so worried that Joel was going to go out in this really dangerous situation.
sentences.zh: 马特非常担心乔尔会去到那种极其危险的境地。

sentences.en: He knows his son is sort of hard-headed, maybe sometimes pushes boundaries.
sentences.zh: 他知道他的儿子有点固执，有时候会挑战界限。

sentences.en: And he knew he couldn't stop Joel from signing up for this work.
sentences.zh: 他也知道自己无法阻止乔尔报名做这份工作。

sentences.en: Joel was determined, but he was really worried.
sentences.zh: 乔尔意志坚定，但他真的很担心。

sentences.en: Understandably.
sentences.zh: 这是可以理解的。

sentences.en: So Steve saw me just nervously pacing and waiting.
sentences.zh: 所以史蒂夫看到我在那儿紧张地踱步等待。

sentences.en: And Steve came up to me and he approached me.
sentences.zh: 然后史蒂夫朝我走过来，他走近了我。

sentences.en: And Steve Dodds, who's the president of Pacific Oasis, comes over and talks to Matt and reassures him.
sentences.zh: “太平洋绿洲”的总裁史蒂夫·多兹走过来跟马特谈话并安慰了他。

sentences.en: And he said, hey, we'll take good care of him.
sentences.zh: 他说，嘿，我们会好好照顾他的。

sentences.en: He's going to be all right.
sentences.zh: 他会没事的。

sentences.en: And anybody could say that, but I truly did believe him.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以这么说，但我确实相信了他。

sentences.en: I respected him.
sentences.zh: 我尊重他。

sentences.en: And then Joel gets in a truck and he drives off to his very first fire.
sentences.zh: 然后乔尔上了卡车，开车驶向他的第一场火灾。

sentences.en: So can you tell us about your first fire?
sentences.zh: 那你能不能跟我们讲讲你的第一场火灾？

sentences.en: It was like California coming to the Oregon border.
sentences.zh: 就像加州蔓延到了俄勒冈州边境一样。

sentences.en: So we were there to like protect it coming into Oregon.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在那里是为了阻止它蔓延进俄勒冈州。

sentences.en: This fire was called the Clamathon fire.
sentences.zh: 这场火灾被称为克拉马松火灾。

sentences.en: Every fire has a name.
sentences.zh: 每场火灾都有一个名字。

sentences.en: So we were doing a lot of direct hand line.
sentences.zh: 所以我们当时在做很多直接的消防隔离带人工开辟工作。

sentences.en: So that's you're at the fire's edge.
sentences.zh: 也就是说你在火灾的边缘。

sentences.en: You're digging down to like bare mineral soil, creating like a small fire break.
sentences.zh: 你一直向下挖到裸露的矿物质土壤，建立一个小型防火隔离带。

sentences.en: The fire stops.
sentences.zh: 火就停了。

sentences.en: So fighting a wildfire is not like what we sort of imagine when we think of firefighting.
sentences.zh: 所以扑灭野火并不像我们想象扑救火灾时的那种样子。

sentences.en: There's not usually water and hoses involved.
sentences.zh: 通常不涉及水和水带。

sentences.en: It's more like you're digging a containment line.
sentences.zh: 更像是你在挖一条遏制线。

sentences.en: I would definitely think that any kind of firefighting required water.
sentences.zh: 我绝对会认为任何种类的消防工作都需要水。

sentences.en: So this is interesting.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, what it is, is that wildfires are too big to put out with water.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，实际情况是，野火太大了，根本无法用水扑灭。

sentences.en: They can really only be trapped and contained.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上只能被围堵和控制。

sentences.en: You're just trying to stop it from spreading on the ground.
sentences.zh: 你只是在试图阻止它在地面上蔓延。

sentences.en: Basically small flames smoldering.
sentences.zh: 基本上是阴燃的小火苗。

sentences.en: But what that means for somebody like Joel is that you're just working right next to the fire in a way that's sort of unbelievable.
sentences.zh: 但对于像乔尔这样的人来说，这意味着你就在火灾旁边工作，这种方式有点让人难以置信。

sentences.en: Joel's first night was basically traipsing around on a cliff's edge right next to the active fire.
sentences.zh: 乔尔的第一晚基本上就是在紧挨着活动火源的悬崖边上磕磕绊绊地走来走去。

sentences.en: The scariest part about that first fire was they call it a freight train.
sentences.zh: 那场火灾最让人害怕的部分是他们称之为货运列车的东西。

sentences.en: You start hearing the fire.
sentences.zh: 你开始听到火的声音。

sentences.en: You can't see it, but you just start hearing trees just torching and running.
sentences.zh: 你看不到它，但你就是开始听到树木被烧焦并迅速蔓延的声音。

sentences.en: It sounds like, yeah, a train.
sentences.zh: 听起来就像，对，一辆火车。

sentences.en: He told me about how he was hearing trees snap.
sentences.zh: 他跟我说起他当时听到树木断裂的声音。

sentences.en: All night long, you know.
sentences.zh: 整整一晚上，你知道的。

sentences.en: So he's crossing checkpoints.
sentences.zh: 所以他穿过了各个检查站。

sentences.en: The National Guard was there.
sentences.zh: 国民警卫队当时就在那儿。

sentences.en: They shut down all highways.
sentences.zh: 他们封闭了所有高速公路。

sentences.en: And he gets to drive around them to go to this sort of off-limits space with his crew.
sentences.zh: 然后他开着车绕过他们，和他的队员一起进入了这种本不允许进入的区域。

sentences.en: I'm like, I thought it was the coolest thing ever, you know.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，我觉得这是有史以来最酷的事情，你知道的。

sentences.en: And it's this wild, unpredictable scene.
sentences.zh: 那是一个疯狂且无法预测的现场。

sentences.en: It's pure chaos, dude.
sentences.zh: 简直是一团糟，老兄。

sentences.en: Flames start ripping, wind changes.
sentences.zh: 火焰开始肆虐，风向变了。

sentences.en: Where he is right next to these flames.
sentences.zh: 他所在的位置紧挨着这些火焰。

sentences.en: Fire on both sides of us.
sentences.zh: 我们两边都是大火。

sentences.en: It's like, I look up, like a 200-foot wall of flames just like 50 feet away from me.
sentences.zh: 就好像，我抬头一看，一堵200英尺高的火墙离我只有大约50英尺远。

sentences.en: And he's starting to get to know these guys who are sort of teaching him how to be out there and stay safe, but also teasing him.
sentences.zh: 他开始结识这些队员，他们教他如何在野外生存并保持安全，同时也取笑他。

sentences.en: My closest friends I met on that first fire.
sentences.zh: 我最要好的朋友是我在那次初次灭火任务中认识的。

sentences.en: You know, I've kept that circle.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我一直维持着这个朋友圈。

sentences.en: For him, it was everything he had hoped it might be to go out and fight a wildfire.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这完全实现了他对外出扑救野火的一切期许。

sentences.en: It sounds like he found that band of brothers element that he was really drawn to.
sentences.zh: 听起来他找到了那种让他非常向往的生死之交的感觉。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So after that, he was pretty much hooked.
sentences.zh: 所以在那之后，他基本上就彻底迷上了。

sentences.en: He worked six more fire seasons.
sentences.zh: 他又参加了六个火灾季的工作。

sentences.en: He learned to work a chainsaw.
sentences.zh: 他学会了操作电锯。

sentences.en: And that meant that he would sort of be out in front of the rest of the crew, leading this group of guys deep into the woods, cutting down trees, cutting down flaming branches.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他通常会走在其余队员的前面，带领这群人深入树林，砍伐树木，砍掉燃烧的树枝。

sentences.en: It took me three, about three years to be able to walk through the woods without falling over, if that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 我花了三年，差不多三年时间，才能在树林里走路而不摔倒，如果这么说你能理解的话。

sentences.en: Like with a chainsaw, with all the weight, it took about three years.
sentences.zh: 就像带着电锯，背着所有的重量，大约花了三年时间。

sentences.en: He would be hiking with a 50-pound pack.
sentences.zh: 他会背着50磅重的背包徒步。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Just, you know, him, his friends, and nature.
sentences.zh: 就是，你知道的，他、他的朋友们，还有大自然。

sentences.en: You're removed from like everyday life.
sentences.zh: 你脱离了日常生活。

sentences.en: I don't like everyday life, personally, so it's like, I like that, you know.
sentences.zh: 我个人不喜欢日常生活，所以我就挺喜欢这种状态的，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's really physically demanding, but it was also for him really rewarding and made him proud.
sentences.zh: 这在体能上要求极高，但对她来说也极具成就感，并让他感到自豪。

sentences.en: He felt like it was finally something that he was just naturally good at.
sentences.zh: 他觉得这终于是一件他生来就很擅长的事情。

sentences.en: It's just freedom.
sentences.zh: 这就是自由。

sentences.en: Being on fire just doesn't feel like a job.
sentences.zh: 在火场上感觉根本不像是在工作。

sentences.en: It's like make-believe stuff that we do out there, you know, it's just fairyland shit, so it's cool.
sentences.zh: 这就像我们在野外玩的那些假装游戏，你知道的，简直就是童话里扯淡的事，所以真的很酷。

sentences.en: But it also involved a lot of risk.
sentences.zh: 但这也伴随着巨大的风险。

sentences.en: He fell down a burning hill once.
sentences.zh: 他有一次从一座燃烧的山坡上滚了下来。

sentences.en: He almost cut into his foot with his chainsaw.
sentences.zh: 他差点用电锯切到自己的脚。

sentences.en: He got full-body poison oak.
sentences.zh: 他全身都长满了毒橡树疹。

sentences.en: And one of the most dangerous things about the work was a natural byproduct of fires, which was breathing in smoke.
sentences.zh: 这项工作最危险的事情之一是火灾的自然副产物，那就是吸入烟雾。

sentences.en: And nobody out there wore masks.
sentences.zh: 而且那里的所有人都不戴口罩。

sentences.en: Why wouldn't they wear masks?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么不戴口罩？

sentences.en: Masks weren't provided when he started this work, and they also weren't allowed.
sentences.zh: 他开始这项工作时没有提供口罩，而且也是不允许戴的。

sentences.en: And this is a long-time Forest Service policy.
sentences.zh: 这是森林服务局长期以来的政策。

sentences.en: And what the Forest Service says is that wearing a mask could increase your risk of heat stroke.
sentences.zh: 森林服务局的说法是，戴口罩可能会增加中暑的风险。

sentences.en: The work is really taxing.
sentences.zh: 这项工作非常消耗体力。

sentences.en: It's usually pretty hot out there.
sentences.zh: 野外通常相当炎热。

sentences.en: And the concern is if you're out there with something over your face, maybe you would start to overheat.
sentences.zh: 人们担心的是，如果你在脸上戴着东西，可能会开始体温过高。

sentences.en: Wildland firefighters in other parts of the world do wear masks, and there has not been a heat stroke issue there.
sentences.zh: 世界其他地方的森林消防员确实会戴口罩，那里并没有出现中暑问题。

sentences.en: But that's what the Forest Service says.
sentences.zh: 但森林服务局就是这么说的。

sentences.en: But there was also this cultural element of not wanting to seem weak.
sentences.zh: 不过其中也有一种不想显得软弱的文化因素。

sentences.en: Firefighters sort of see masks as, like, silly, as a sign that you're not going to be up to the job.
sentences.zh: 消防员觉得口罩有点傻，是无法胜任这份工作的标志。

sentences.en: And breathing in smoke is seen as a sign that you're willing to, you know, take sacrifices and focus on the work at hand.
sentences.zh: 而吸入烟雾则被视为你愿意做出牺牲、专注于手头工作的标志。

sentences.en: And you're not going to get too caught up in your own comfort.
sentences.zh: 你不会过分纠结于自身的舒适度。

sentences.en: So basically, even if they had been provided with masks, what you're saying is that they probably wouldn't have worn them because of this culture.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，即使发了口罩，你的意思是由于这种文化，他们也可能不会戴。

sentences.en: Yeah, there is this macho fireline culture.
sentences.zh: 是的，这里存在一种大男子主义的消防前线文化。

sentences.en: But I also think it's worth noting that at this point, firefighters like Joel weren't told that there was any reason to be concerned about smoke.
sentences.zh: 但我也觉得值得一提的是，当时像乔尔这样的消防员并没有被告知有任何理由需要担心烟雾。

sentences.en: So part of it maybe is that they thought that the masks could make them look weak,
sentences.zh: 所以部分原因可能是他们觉得戴口罩会让自己看起来很弱，

sentences.en: but they also maybe just had no reason to think that there would be a real benefit to wearing them.
sentences.zh: 但他们也可能只是找不到任何理由觉得戴口罩会有什么真正的益处。

sentences.en: But the smoke exposure was really intense.
sentences.zh: 但烟雾的暴露情况确实非常严重。

sentences.en: Pacific Oasis workers told me that morning sounded like an emphysema clinic in their fire camps.
sentences.zh: “太平洋绿洲”的工人告诉我，那天早上火灾营地里的声音听起来就像一家肺气肿诊所。

sentences.en: They were coughing.
sentences.zh: 他们在咳嗽。

sentences.en: They had black stuff coming out their noses.
sentences.zh: 他们的鼻子里流出黑色的东西。

sentences.en: There's something called camp cred that goes around these fire camps where everyone will be coughing and everyone will be sort of feeling sick.
sentences.zh: 这些火灾营地里流传着一种叫“营地信誉”的东西，每个人都在咳嗽，每个人都觉得身体不舒服。

sentences.en: And people just think of it as like a natural consequence of the work.
sentences.zh: 人们只是把这当作工作的自然结果。

sentences.en: For Joel, it was sort of like being sore.
sentences.zh: 对乔尔来说，这有点像肌肉酸痛。

sentences.en: It was just something that he thought came along with fighting fires.
sentences.zh: 这只是他认为扑救山火必然会伴随的东西。

sentences.en: And for him, it was proof that he was doing something right and he was putting in the right amount of effort.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这证明了他做对了事，付出了正确的努力。

sentences.en: He was really focused on trying to get his boss Steve's attention and show Steve that he was tough and he should be sent out on more fires and maybe promoted.
sentences.zh: 他非常专注于试图引起老板史蒂夫的注意，向史蒂夫证明自己很顽强，应该被派去执行更多灭火任务，甚至可能得到晋升。

sentences.en: So he was working really hard.
sentences.zh: 所以他工作非常努力。

sentences.en: He was trying to impress Steve, show Steve that he would make any sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 他试图给史蒂夫留下深刻印象，向史蒂夫证明他愿意做出任何牺牲。

sentences.en: He would cough up black stuff.
sentences.zh: 他会咳出黑色的东西。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Go out for weeks and weeks without complaining.
sentences.zh: 一连出去好几个星期都不抱怨。

sentences.en: And he was getting these positive reviews.
sentences.zh: 而且他得到了这些积极的评价。

sentences.en: Steve seemed to be liking what he was doing and eventually Steve invited him to start training to be a crew boss, which meant that he would lead his own team of about 20 people.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫似乎很喜欢他的表现，最终史蒂夫邀请他开始接受培训成为一名领班，这意味着他将领导自己大约20人的团队。

sentences.en: And that, for Joel, was one of the proudest moments of his life.
sentences.zh: 对乔尔来说，那是他一生中最自豪的时刻之一。

sentences.en: It was so validating.
sentences.zh: 这种认可意义重大。

sentences.en: Did you imagine spending your whole career in fire?
sentences.zh: 你想过把整个职业生涯都奉献给消防事业吗？

sentences.en: Oh yeah, I already knew I was in, yeah.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的，我当时就知道我入行了，是的。

sentences.en: I knew that's a job I wanted probably when I was 19.
sentences.zh: 我大概在19岁时就知道这是我想干的工作。

sentences.en: I was probably going to stick with that one.
sentences.zh: 我大概会一直干下去。

sentences.en: You know, I'm good at it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我很擅长。

sentences.en: I'm really good at it.
sentences.zh: 我真的很擅长。

sentences.en: And he started to see this as probably being his lifelong career.
sentences.zh: 他开始认为这很可能是他终生的职业。

sentences.en: And that's why what happened next felt like such a betrayal.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么接下来发生的事情感觉像是一种背叛。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了“连线”游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏板块的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖尔斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责制作“拼写蜜蜂”和“字谜框”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的奇特现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到声音的那几位一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com斜杠games，今天就开始游戏吧。

sentences.en: So Hannah, it sounds like Joel is basically living his dream life.
sentences.zh: 所以汉娜，听起来乔尔基本上过着他梦想中的生活。

sentences.en: When do things start taking a turn for the worse for him?
sentences.zh: 他的生活从什么时候开始急转直下的？

sentences.en: Yeah, so looking back at it, I had a lot of different signs.
sentences.zh: 对，所以回想起来，我当时有很多不同的征兆。

sentences.en: Everything started falling apart last year.
sentences.zh: 一切在去年开始瓦解。

sentences.en: It was the 4th of July weekend.
sentences.zh: 那是7月4日的周末。

sentences.en: You know, I was extremely, probably the best shape I've ever been in my life before that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我极其健康，那可能是我一生中状态最好的时候。

sentences.en: You know, I just did my crew boss class.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我刚完成了领班培训课程。

sentences.en: He was fighting a fire in Northern California, staying in a hotel.
sentences.zh: 他当时在加利福尼亚州北部灭火，住在一家酒店里。

sentences.en: I broke out in a rash.
sentences.zh: 我起了一身皮疹。

sentences.en: He had this strange rash that was sort of creeping up his legs.
sentences.zh: 他身上长了一种奇怪的皮疹，正顺着腿部向上蔓延。

sentences.en: It was so painful, dude.
sentences.zh: 疼得要命，老兄。

sentences.en: And I didn't know what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我当时不知道是怎么回事。

sentences.en: It really hurt.
sentences.zh: 真的很痛。

sentences.en: It looked like nothing he'd ever seen before.
sentences.zh: 这看起来跟他以前见过的任何东西都不同。

sentences.en: But he didn't want to complain.
sentences.zh: 但他不想抱怨。

sentences.en: And we're staying in hotels, right?
sentences.zh: 我们住在酒店里，对吧？

sentences.en: So everybody was like, oh, you got bed bugs.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都说，哦，你惹上臭虫了。

sentences.en: And everybody was like freaking out.
sentences.zh: 每个人都吓坏了。

sentences.en: And so he let it slide.
sentences.zh: 所以他就不了了之了。

sentences.en: Then his crew moves deep into the foreSt.
sentences.zh: 然后他的队员深入森林。

sentences.en: And they start camping there to get closer to the fire line.
sentences.zh: 他们开始在那里露营，以便更靠近火线。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: Day 9 or 10, my face started to like droop.
sentences.zh: 第9天或第10天，我的脸开始下垂。

sentences.en: That's when his crewmates noticed that his face is drooping.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，他的队友注意到他的脸在下垂。

sentences.en: Half of his mouth is sort of just hanging open.
sentences.zh: 他的一半嘴巴基本上就那么张着。

sentences.en: And again, he wants to be seen as this, you know, tough person who could be a crew boss.
sentences.zh: 同样，他希望被看作是一个你知道的、能胜任领班的坚强的人。

sentences.en: And so he keeps going working these 12-hour shifts until the end of their deployment.
sentences.zh: 所以他继续坚持上这些12小时的班，直到部署结束。

sentences.en: That's when a medic finally sees him and says, you need to get to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，一名医护人员终于看到了他并说，你得去医院。

sentences.en: You might have had a stroke.
sentences.zh: 你可能中风了。

sentences.en: Were people worried about him?
sentences.zh: 大家当时为他担心吗？

sentences.en: Do we know during the period that he's working with a drooping face?
sentences.zh: 在我们所知的他带着下垂的脸工作的那段时期里？

sentences.en: You know, people noticed it, but nobody was that worried.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，大家注意到了，但没有人那么担心。

sentences.en: And I think that partly goes back to this fire line culture.
sentences.zh: 我想这部分要归咎于这种消防前线文化。

sentences.en: I mean, firefighters say if you get injured out on the fire line, you just rub dirt in it and keep walking.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，消防员说如果你在火线上受伤，你就在上面抹点泥土继续走。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So everybody is just very focused on getting this fire under control and keeping going, sort of no matter what happens.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都非常专注于控制火势并继续前进，基本上不管发生什么事。

sentences.en: So the medic tells him, you need urgent medical attention.
sentences.zh: 所以医护人员告诉他，你需要紧急医疗救助。

sentences.en: Does he go to a hospital?
sentences.zh: 他去医院了吗？

sentences.en: Does he heed that advice?
sentences.zh: 他听从那个建议了吗？

sentences.en: So Joel opts not to take an ambulance.
sentences.zh: 所以乔尔选择不坐救护车。

sentences.en: He instead is driven by Steve, the owner of the company.
sentences.zh: 相反，他由公司老板史蒂夫开车送走。

sentences.en: And in my impression, I'm going to the hospital, right?
sentences.zh: 在我的印象中，我要去医院，对吧？

sentences.en: He thinks that Steve is going to take him to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 他以为史蒂夫要带他去医院。

sentences.en: That's sort of the protocol for a moment like that.
sentences.zh: 那种时刻通常是这样的流程。

sentences.en: Instead, he was driven 90 minutes back from the fire line.
sentences.zh: 相反，他被载着从火线开了90分钟的车送了回去。

sentences.en: And then he's surprised because Steve drops him off at his dad's house.
sentences.zh: 然后他很惊讶，因为史蒂夫把他放在了他爸爸家门口。

sentences.en: It's almost midnight at this point.
sentences.zh: 当时已经快半夜了。

sentences.en: He looks drawn.
sentences.zh: 他看起来面容憔悴。

sentences.en: He looks weak.
sentences.zh: 他看起来很虚弱。

sentences.en: You could have asked me what color this guy was, and I probably didn't know.
sentences.zh: 你当时问我这家伙脸色是什么样，我可能都答不上来。

sentences.en: That's how just messed up I was.
sentences.zh: 我当时就是被折腾成那个鬼样子的。

sentences.en: You know, my body was just shutting down.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的身体当时已经彻底垮了。

sentences.en: When I saw him in that state, I knew this isn't a cold.
sentences.zh: 当我看到他那副样子时，我知道这根本不是感冒。

sentences.en: And his dad realizes something's terribly wrong here.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲也意识到情况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: I drove him to the hospital thinking that he's going to die at any moment.
sentences.zh: 我开车送他去医院，心里想着他随时都可能会死。

sentences.en: I knew it.
sentences.zh: 我当时就知道了。

sentences.en: And immediately takes him to the emergency room.
sentences.zh: 然后立刻把他送进了急诊室。

sentences.en: There's no going back from something like that happening as a parent.
sentences.zh: 作为父母，经历过这种事之后，就再也回不到从前了。

sentences.en: So at the hospital, doctors start running tests, and it takes a few days of tests, and Joel is getting weaker and weaker.
sentences.zh: 所以在医院里，医生开始给他做各种检查，经过几天的检查，乔尔的身体一天比一天虚弱。

sentences.en: At this point, he can't even really walk down the hallway.
sentences.zh: 到了这个时候，他甚至连走廊都快走不动了。

sentences.en: And eventually, they come back with an answer that nobody expects.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们给出了一个谁也没料到的结果。

sentences.en: He is diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia, which is an aggressive blood cancer that is most often seen in people in their 60s and 70s.
sentences.zh: 他被确诊患有急性髓系白血病，这是一种侵袭性血癌，最常见于六七十岁的人群。

sentences.en: Not somebody Joel's age.
sentences.zh: 根本不是乔尔这个年纪的人会得的。

sentences.en: And how old was he at that point?
sentences.zh: 那他当时多大？

sentences.en: He is diagnosed the day before he turns 25.
sentences.zh: 他在25岁生日前一天被确诊。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: That moment, it's still in shock for him.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，对他来说仍然像是一场震惊。

sentences.en: So it feels fake.
sentences.zh: 感觉太不真实了。

sentences.en: But it's not, you know.
sentences.zh: 但这一切都是真的。

sentences.en: He needs immediate chemotherapy, immediate blood transfusions.
sentences.zh: 他需要立即接受化疗和输血。

sentences.en: That rash that was creeping up his legs turns out to have been his blood basically just breaking down.
sentences.zh: 他腿上蔓延开来的那些皮疹，原来基本上就是他的血液在崩溃。

sentences.en: Without treatment, he could die within a matter of weeks.
sentences.zh: 如果不接受治疗，他可能会在短短几周内死亡。

sentences.en: And the truth is, even with medical interventions, only about half of patients with this kind of cancer survive a year.
sentences.zh: 事实是，即使进行了医学干预，这种癌症患者能活过一年的也只有大约一半。

sentences.en: But all Joel is thinking about in these days is how quickly he can get through treatment and get back to fighting fires.
sentences.zh: 但乔尔这段时间心里想的，全都是自己能多快完成治疗，然后重返消防岗位。

sentences.en: So I was really excited, man, to go back with that crew.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时真的很兴奋，伙计，能和那个团队一起回去。

sentences.en: I was locked in with that crew.
sentences.zh: 我当时全身心都投入到了那个团队里。

sentences.en: But it was a good crew.
sentences.zh: 但那确实是个不错的团队。

sentences.en: They got the most hours out of any of the crews, you know.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作时长是所有团队里最多的。

sentences.en: He's sort of not understanding how serious the situation is, how in danger he is of dying.
sentences.zh: 他有点不明白情况有多严重，自己离死亡有多近。

sentences.en: And he's just focused on this life that he thought was in front of him.
sentences.zh: 他只专注於他原本以为在前方等着他的生活。

sentences.en: It sounds like he almost couldn't accept the reality of what was actually happening to his body.
sentences.zh: 听起来他几乎无法接受自己身体正在发生这种现实的打击。

sentences.en: Yes, I mean, it's so jarring for him.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这对他的打击太震撼了。

sentences.en: Like, he just can't really process what's going on.
sentences.zh: 就像，他真的无法消化到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: But for his father, the reality was very clear.
sentences.zh: 但对他的父亲来说，现实是非常残酷的。

sentences.en: And he was thinking back to that first day when he dropped off Joel and Steve said that he would take care of his son.
sentences.zh: 他回想起送乔尔去的那第一天，史蒂夫曾说会照顾好他的儿子。

sentences.en: He got dropped off at my doorstep by the same person not seven years prior had told me, hey, we're going to take care of him.
sentences.zh: 就在不到七年前，正是同一个人把他送到我家门口，对我说，嘿，我们会照顾好他的。

sentences.en: For his part, Steve says that he understood that this was going to be a long diagnostic process for Joel.
sentences.zh: 史蒂夫则表示，他当时明白这对乔尔来说将是一个漫长的诊断过程。

sentences.en: It wasn't going to be a quick thing.
sentences.zh: 这不是一件能快快了结的事。

sentences.en: And he was trying to do Joel a favor.
sentences.zh: 他当时其实是想帮乔尔一个忙。

sentences.en: By letting him rest at home and then go into the hospital the next day.
sentences.zh: 让他先在家休息，第二天再去医院。

sentences.en: But Matt just cannot get over that moment, that nightmare moment of seeing your child.
sentences.zh: 但马特始终无法释怀那个时刻，那个看到自己孩子遭遇噩梦般的时刻。

sentences.en: He felt like on death's door and they're being taken to your house instead of taken to get medical care.
sentences.zh: 他觉得孩子当时已经一只脚踏进鬼门关了，而他们却被带回了家，而不是去接受医疗救治。

sentences.en: They let him linger out there having facial paralysis, drooling and all this stuff going on.
sentences.zh: 他们任由他在那里拖着，面部瘫痪、流口水，还发生着各种各样的情况。

sentences.en: He had no control over his muscles.
sentences.zh: 他根本无法控制自己的肌肉。

sentences.en: Pain.
sentences.zh: 痛苦不堪。

sentences.en: He wasn't okay.
sentences.zh: 他当时状况很不好。

sentences.en: And what happened to him really could have happened at any private firefighting company.
sentences.zh: 而且他遭遇的事情，其实在任何一家私人消防公司都可能发生。

sentences.en: No matter who he worked for, he would probably have been out there without a mask, in heavy smoke, and he might have ended up in this exact situation at the hospital,
sentences.zh: 无论他为谁工作，他可能都会在没有面罩的情况下置身于浓烟之中，并且最终可能会在医院落得和现在一模一样的下场，

sentences.en: sick with cancer.
sentences.zh: 身患癌症。

sentences.en: But I think that for Matt and eventually for Joel, they got really fixated on these specifics of where he got dropped off, what time it was,
sentences.zh: 但我觉得，对于马特以及后来的乔尔来说，他们变得非常执着于那些细节，比如他是在哪里被送下的，当时是几点，

sentences.en: because they felt like Joel was just sort of dumped, like he had been a disposable worker all along.
sentences.zh: 因为他们觉得乔尔就像是被随手抛弃了一样，仿佛他一直都只是个用完即弃的工人。

sentences.en: And so they felt really mad.
sentences.zh: 所以他们感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, all of these medical bills started to come in.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，所有的医疗账单开始雪片般飞来。

sentences.en: I was paying that first hospital bill.
sentences.zh: 我当时在付第一笔医院账单。

sentences.en: I didn't have insurance.
sentences.zh: 我没有保险。

sentences.en: I was paying that shit out of my pocket, right?
sentences.zh: 我特么都是自掏腰包付的，对吧？

sentences.en: He and Matt felt like Pacific Oasis should be held accountable since he had gotten sick on their watch.
sentences.zh: 他和马特都觉得“太平洋绿洲”公司应该承担责任，因为他是因为在他们手下工作才生病的。

sentences.en: And workers' compensation covers things like lost wages and hospital bills when employees get sick on the job.
sentences.zh: 而工伤赔偿涵盖了员工因公生病时的工资损失和医疗账单等费用。

sentences.en: So Joel and Matt decide they are going to file a workers' compensation claim.
sentences.zh: 于是乔尔和马特决定申请工伤索赔。

sentences.en: They go down to Pacific Oasis, and Steve pulls them into a room.
sentences.zh: 他们来到“太平洋绿洲”公司，史蒂夫把他们拉进了一个房间。

sentences.en: And said, there's no way you guys can prove this is work-related.
sentences.zh: 然后说，你们绝对没有办法证明这跟工作有关。

sentences.en: And I said, what?
sentences.zh: 我说，什么？

sentences.en: He basically said anything could have caused this.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是说任何事情都可能导致这个结果。

sentences.en: Our workers' compensation policy is not going to pay for this.
sentences.zh: 我们的工伤保险政策是不会为此买单的。

sentences.en: I'm not trying to prove anything.
sentences.zh: 我不是想证明什么。

sentences.en: I'm just trying to say that this happened to him on a fire.
sentences.zh: 我只是想说这是他在灭火时遭遇的。

sentences.en: Let's get him covered right now until we can figure this out.
sentences.zh: 让我们先把他的医疗费用报销了，直到我们弄清楚这件事。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: But they filed the claim anyway, and ultimately the workers' comp insurer denies their claim.
sentences.zh: 但他们还是提交了索赔，最终工伤保险公司拒绝了他们的索赔。

sentences.en: So I was just using money out of pocket, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以我基本上只能自掏腰包。

sentences.en: Out of pocket.
sentences.zh: 自掏腰包。

sentences.en: And why couldn't they prove this link?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们无法证明这种联系？

sentences.en: It's almost impossible to prove that any individual cancer case comes from wildfire smoke.
sentences.zh: 要证明任何个别的癌症病例是由野火烟雾引起的，几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: And that sort of shields the whole firefighting industry from responsibility.
sentences.zh: 这某种程度上保护了整个消防行业免于承担责任。

sentences.en: People who work at the Forest Service have told me that this is one reason that firefighters historically have not been provided with masks.
sentences.zh: 森林管理局的工作人员曾告诉我，这也是为什么历史上消防员一直没有配备面罩的原因之一。

sentences.en: Because if you give somebody a mask, it's essentially acknowledging that smoke is risky and could cause some sort of long-term illness.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你给某人发一个面罩，基本上就等於承认了烟雾是有风险的，并且可能导致某种长期疾病。

sentences.en: We're not going to give you a mask that could protect you because that would be an admission that you are in danger doing this work.
sentences.zh: 我们不会给你提供能保护你的面罩，因为那将等于承认你在进行这项工作时身处危险之中。

sentences.en: So therefore, we were going to leave you unprotected.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们打算让你处于毫无保护的状态。

sentences.en: This is what whistleblowers have been telling me, that there's just sort of been this culture of denial around how dangerous smoke is.
sentences.zh: 这就是内部举报人一直对我说的话，关于烟雾有多危险这一点，一直存在着一种否认的文化。

sentences.en: Because what do you do once you acknowledge that?
sentences.zh: 因为一旦你承认了这一点，你该怎么办？

sentences.en: You have to really change how fires are fought.
sentences.zh: 你必须彻底改变灭火的方式。

sentences.en: The government might start to have to provide more staffing so that people could take breaks from smoke.
sentences.zh: 政府可能不得不开始提供更多的人员配备，以便人们可以轮流从烟雾中抽身休息。

sentences.en: And they might have to start covering this whole range of health conditions.
sentences.zh: 而且他们可能不得不开始承保这一整套的健康状况。

sentences.en: Okay, so the employers don't acknowledge a link between the work and the illness here.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以雇主不承认工作与这里的疾病之间存在联系。

sentences.en: But is there a link between the work and the type of cancer that Joel got?
sentences.zh: 但是，工作与乔尔得的这种癌症之间真的有联系吗？

sentences.en: Like, what do we know about that for sure?
sentences.zh: 比如说，我们对此到底了解多少？

sentences.en: So until the 1980s, people thought that wildfire smoke was basically benign, like a campfire.
sentences.zh: 所以在20世纪80年代之前，人们认为野火烟雾基本上是无害的，就像营火一样。

sentences.en: But since then, there's been a lot of research that has shown pretty definitively that wildfire smoke is linked to cardiovascular issues, lung issues,
sentences.zh: 但从那以后，有大量的研究非常明确地表明，野火烟雾与心血管问题、肺部问题有关，

sentences.en: and at least 12 kinds of cancers.
sentences.zh: 并且至少与12种癌症有关。

sentences.en: So responding to this growing body of research, in 2022,
sentences.zh: 因此，为了应对这日益增多的研究成果，在2022年，

sentences.en: Congress actually forced the Forest Service to start offering workers' compensation benefits for a list of more than a dozen cancers that are most strongly associated with smoke exposure.
sentences.zh: 国会实际上迫使森林管理局开始为一份包含十多种与烟雾暴露最密切相关的癌症名单提供工伤赔偿福利。

sentences.en: But that's not how it works for this large group of other firefighters working on contract for the Forest Service, but working for private companies.
sentences.zh: 但对于为森林管理局承包、却受雇于私营公司的这大批其他消防员来说，情况并非如此。

sentences.en: So basically, if you work directly for the federal government fighting fires, you will get coverage.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，如果你直接为联邦政府从事灭火工作，你就会获得保障。

sentences.en: But if you work for a private company that works for the Forest Service, you will not get coverage.
sentences.zh: 但如果你为受雇于森林管理局的私营公司工作，你将无法获得保障。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So if you've had, you know, Joel's career, and then you develop leukemia, and you're working for the Forest Service, you now don't have to prove where your cancer came from.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你经历了，你知道的，乔尔的职业生涯，然后你得了白血病，而你当时在森林管理局工作，你现在就不必证明你的癌症是从哪里来的。

sentences.en: It's just assumed that it came from your work on fires because there's such a strong link.
sentences.zh: 大家会直接认为它来自于你在火灾中的工作，因为这二者有着如此强烈的联系。

sentences.en: But for Joel, he would have to prove where his cancer came from, which is almost impossible.
sentences.zh: 但对于乔尔来说，他必须证明他的癌症是从哪里来的，而这几乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: So basically, for somebody like Joel, he is completely on his own, it sounds like, to cover the cost of his treatment.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，对于像乔尔这样的人来说，听起来他只能完全靠自己来承担治疗费用。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And as you can imagine, it was extremely expensive.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，这极其昂贵。

sentences.en: The family spent basically everything they had trying to pay for this.
sentences.zh: 这个家庭几乎花光了他们所有的积蓄来支付这些费用。

sentences.en: And how was Joel doing through all of this?
sentences.zh: 那乔尔在这期间情况怎么样？

sentences.en: Was the treatment working?
sentences.zh: 治疗起作用了吗？

sentences.en: The chemotherapy starts to fight back the cancer, but it takes a tremendous physical toll on Joel.
sentences.zh: 化疗开始对抗癌症，但这给乔尔的身体带来了巨大的摧残。

sentences.en: He could barely move.
sentences.zh: 他几乎动弹不得。

sentences.en: He was in pain all the time.
sentences.zh: 他无时无刻不在承受着痛苦。

sentences.en: He would crawl up to his attic bedroom on hands and knees.
sentences.zh: 他只能手脚并用地爬上他那位于阁楼的卧室。

sentences.en: By the winter, though, he started to get better.
sentences.zh: 不过到了冬天，他的情况开始好转。

sentences.en: His cancer went into remission, and he started recovering a little bit of strength.
sentences.zh: 他的癌症进入了缓解期，体力也开始恢复了一点。

sentences.en: He went out with his father to try to go on a hike like he used to do with him.
sentences.zh: 他和父亲一起外出，试图像过去那样去远足。

sentences.en: And at first, he could only take these sort of stuttering steps.
sentences.zh: 起初，他只能迈出那种踉踉跄跄的步伐。

sentences.en: But little by little, he was able to recover a little bit of who he had been.
sentences.zh: 但渐渐地，他能够找回一点过去的自己了。

sentences.en: It sounds like he beat the odds.
sentences.zh: 听起来他战胜了死神。

sentences.en: I mean, he went into remission.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他的病情确实缓解了。

sentences.en: His doctors were very careful to explain that the cancer could come back at any time, and it often does.
sentences.zh: 他的主治医生非常谨慎地解释说，癌症随时可能复发，而且这种情况经常发生。

sentences.en: And if it did come back, chemotherapy wouldn't be enough.
sentences.zh: 如果癌症复发，化疗将远远不够。

sentences.en: He would have to have a bone marrow transplant.
sentences.zh: 他必须进行骨髓移植。

sentences.en: But after Joel got the sign-off from his doctors in the spring, he sort of went back to that place of aimlessness that he had been in after graduating high school.
sentences.zh: 但在春季获得医生的许可后，乔尔又回到了高中毕业后那种漫无目的的状态。

sentences.en: He didn't quite know what to do.
sentences.zh: 他不太知道自己该做些什么。

sentences.en: He felt adrift, and his mind started drifting back to fighting fires.
sentences.zh: 他感到漂泊不定，脑海里开始不由自主地回想起灭火的工作。

sentences.en: He started sort of fantasizing about, like, what if I went back there?
sentences.zh: 他开始产生一些幻想，比如，如果我回去了会怎么样？

sentences.en: He wanted to go back to the line.
sentences.zh: 他想回到火线上去。

sentences.en: He wanted to go back to the line.
sentences.zh: 他想回到一线去。

sentences.en: It's where his friends are.
sentences.zh: 那里有他的朋友们。

sentences.en: It's a way to start making money to pay off his debts.
sentences.zh: 这是开始赚钱还债的一种方式。

sentences.en: And Joel is very hung up on that last fire that he fought and how he got sick, and he wasn't able to keep going.
sentences.zh: 乔尔对他的最后那次灭火任务以及他是如何生病的、没能坚持下去这件事一直耿耿于怀。

sentences.en: He really sees that as a defeat.
sentences.zh: 他真的把那视为一种失败。

sentences.en: And in a lot of ways, he says he wants to redeem himself by getting back out on the fire line.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，他说他想通过重返火线来为自己挽回尊严。

sentences.en: Sure, I'm motivated.
sentences.zh: 当然，我是有动力的。

sentences.en: I can go do a fire.
sentences.zh: 我可以去灭火。

sentences.en: But can I do a 14-day run?
sentences.zh: 但我能坚持14天的连轴转吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Well, we try until I die again.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那就拼到我再次倒下为止。

sentences.en: You know, that's one of those things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: He actually went and asked Steve for his job back.
sentences.zh: 他甚至真的去找史蒂夫要求复职。

sentences.en: And Steve told him, are you crazy?
sentences.zh: 而史蒂夫对他说，你疯了吗？

sentences.en: You think that firefighting gave you this cancer?
sentences.zh: 你觉得是消防工作让你得了这种癌症？

sentences.en: You're going to go back?
sentences.zh: 你还要回去？

sentences.en: Isn't that tempting fate?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是在向命运发出挑战吗？

sentences.en: So Steve wouldn't hire him.
sentences.zh: 所以史蒂夫不肯雇佣他。

sentences.en: He couldn't get a job locally.
sentences.zh: 他在当地找不到工作。

sentences.en: So he bought a ticket to go to Alaska, where there are a lot more federal, wildland firefighting jobs.
sentences.zh: 于是他买了一张去阿拉斯加的机票，那里有更多联邦的森林野火消防工作。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And Matt desperately wants Joel to do any kind of work besides firefighting.
sentences.zh: 马特极度希望乔尔去做除了消防之外的任何工作。

sentences.en: But he also knows that if he pushes too hard, he could alienate Joel.
sentences.zh: 但他也知道，如果逼得太紧，可能会把乔尔推得更远。

sentences.en: So he's walking this really fine line.
sentences.zh: 所以他走得非常小心谨慎。

sentences.en: You know, everybody's telling me I'm insane.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，每个人都告诉我我疯了。

sentences.en: But I don't care what anybody thinks.
sentences.zh: 但我不在乎别人怎么想。

sentences.en: Like, at the end of the day, it's just all I know.
sentences.zh: 说到底，这只是我唯一擅长的行当。

sentences.en: His kind of cancer is very aggressive.
sentences.zh: 他的这种癌症非常具有侵袭性。

sentences.en: It doesn't have a great prognosis.
sentences.zh: 预后情况不太乐观。

sentences.en: In his mind, he is likely still to die from this cancer.
sentences.zh: 在他心里，他可能仍然觉得自己会死于这种癌症。

sentences.en: If I got a year left in my life, I'm going to do the last year doing some shit I'd enjoy, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我只剩一年寿命，我会在最后一年做点自己喜欢的事，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, the damage is already done, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，伤害已经造成了，对吧？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对。

sentences.en: I mean, it's too late to turn back.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在回头已经太晚了。

sentences.en: I mean, shit.
sentences.zh: 我是说，操。

sentences.en: He feels like everything he's doing now is just sort of borrowed time.
sentences.zh: 他觉得他现在做的一切都像是借来的时间。

sentences.en: And if he ends up dying in his 20s, he wants to just keep going and keep being that strong firefighter.
sentences.zh: 如果他最终在二十多岁时去世，他只想继续坚持下去，继续做那个坚强的消防员。

sentences.en: It really strikes me that there will always be a Joel.
sentences.zh: 这让我深有感触，那就是永远都会有一个乔尔。

sentences.en: There will always be people who need this kind of work, who want to do this kind of work, and an industry that needs Joels, right?
sentences.zh: 总会有这样的人，他们需要这种工作，想要做这种工作，还有一个需要乔尔们的行业，对吧？

sentences.en: It's true.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: There are tens of thousands of wildland firefighters.
sentences.zh: 有数万名森林消防员。

sentences.en: And as wildfire season grows longer and the fires grow more intense, the government is increasingly turning to firefighters like Joel.
sentences.zh: 随着野火季越来越长，火势越来越猛烈，政府越来越依赖像乔尔这样的消防员。

sentences.en: And people get into this work young.
sentences.zh: 人们很年轻就从事这项工作。

sentences.en: They really want to do it.
sentences.zh: 他们是真心想做。

sentences.en: And when they get sick, the industry just sort of moves on.
sentences.zh: 而当他们生病时，这个行业却只是向前看，把他们抛在身后。

sentences.en: And there's always going to be another young person to come and replace them.
sentences.zh: 总会有另一个年轻人来取代他们。

sentences.en: Hannah, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 汉娜，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，蕾切尔。

sentences.en: Not long after Hannah published the first story in this investigative series,
sentences.zh: 在这篇调查报道发表后不久，

sentences.en: Congress held oversight hearings citing her reporting and pressured the agency to make changes.
sentences.zh: 国会举行了监督听证会，引用了她的报道并向机构施压要求其作出改变。

sentences.en: And soon after, it did, reversing its decades-long ban on masks and announcing it will provide masks to all of its firefighters and encourage them to use them.
sentences.zh: 不久之后，它确实照做了，推翻了持续数十年的口罩禁令，并宣布将向所有消防员提供口罩并鼓励他们使用。

sentences.en: No plans have been announced to extend worker compensation coverage to contract firefighters.
sentences.zh: 目前尚未宣布将合同工消防员纳入工伤赔偿范围的任何计划。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Prime Minister Andrew Holness of Jamaica ordered mandatory evacuations and issued dire safety warnings as Hurricane Melissa,
sentences.zh: 牙买加总理安德鲁·霍尔尼斯下令强制疏散并发布了严厉的安全警告，因为飓风“梅丽莎”

sentences.en: with winds of 175 miles per hour and enough moisture to drop nearly three feet of rain, churned towards his country and its 2.8 million people on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一携带着每小时175英里的风速以及足以带来近三英尺降雨的水汽，正翻滚着向该国及其280万人口逼近。

sentences.en: Dangerous winds, catastrophic flooding, and a storm surge as high as 13 feet were expected in Jamaica as soon as Monday night,
sentences.zh: 预计牙买加最早在周一晚间就会遭遇危险的风力、毁灭性的洪水以及高达13英尺的风暴潮，

sentences.en: long before the hurricane's expected landfall on Tuesday morning.
sentences.zh: 远早于飓风预计在周二早晨的登陆时间。
